# hosttracker_maintenance (Resource)

A maintenance window: a span during which planned downtime is held out of the alerting, of the uptime statistics, or of both.

The window's length is given once - as `to` or as `duration_sec`, never both - and its coverage is given once as well: `monitor_ids` with one `suppress` when every monitor is treated the same, or `monitors` when they are not. Both spellings are read back whichever one was written.

Every optional attribute is also computed, because the API reads an absent member as "leave this alone" rather than as "clear this".

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A Sunday-night database window that holds back both the alerting and
# the statistics for every monitor it covers. The end is given as a
# length; `to` is read back derived from it.
resource "hosttracker_maintenance" "weekly_database" {
  name         = "Weekly database maintenance"
  from         = 1785712608
  duration_sec = 3600
  timezone     = "Europe/Berlin"

  recurrence = {
    week_days = ["Sunday"]
  }

  monitor_ids = [
    hosttracker_monitor.marketing.id,
    hosttracker_monitor.api.id,
  ]

  suppress = {
    alerts = true
    stats  = true
  }
}

# A one-off deploy window that treats its monitors differently: the
# marketing site is silenced outright, while the API only stays out of the
# uptime figures. The end is given as an instant here.
resource "hosttracker_maintenance" "deploy" {
  name     = "Release 4.2"
  from     = 1785712608
  to       = 1785714408
  timezone = "Europe/Berlin"

  monitors = [
    {
      monitor_id = hosttracker_monitor.marketing.id
      suppress   = { alerts = true, stats = true }
    },
    {
      monitor_id = hosttracker_monitor.api.id
      suppress   = { alerts = false, stats = true }
    },
  ]
}

resource "hosttracker_monitor" "marketing" {
  type      = "http"
  url       = "https://example.com/"
  name      = "Marketing site"
  locations = { pools = ["allworld"] }
}

resource "hosttracker_monitor" "api" {
  type      = "http"
  url       = "https://api.example.com/health"
  name      = "API"
  locations = { pools = ["allworld"] }
}

output "deploy_window_ends" {
  # Instants are Unix seconds; the RFC 3339 twin is there to be read.
  value = hosttracker_maintenance.deploy.to_rfc3339
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `from` (Number) When the window opens, in Unix seconds.
- `name` (String) A display name. Never an identifier.

### Optional

- `duration_sec` (Number) How long the window lasts, in seconds of real elapsed time. Give the length once, as this or as `to`.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the window is in force. A disabled window suppresses nothing.
- `monitor_ids` (Set of String) The monitors the window covers, all of them getting the `suppress` written beside this attribute. Writing it replaces the coverage rather than adding to it. Use `monitors` instead when the window treats its monitors differently.
- `monitors` (Attributes Set) The window's coverage stated per monitor, for a window that holds back alerting for one monitor and only the statistics for another. Writing it replaces the whole coverage. It is also what a read fills in whichever spelling was written, because it is the shape the window is stored in. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--monitors))
- `recurrence` (Attributes) How the window repeats. Unset, it happens once. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--recurrence))
- `suppress` (Attributes) What the window holds back for the monitors in `monitor_ids`. At least one of the two must be true - a window that suppresses neither does nothing. Read back only while every covered monitor agrees; where they differ, the answer is in `monitors`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--suppress))
- `timezone` (String) The zone the window's wall clock is read in, as an IANA id (`Europe/Berlin`). A Windows spelling is refused with the id to send instead.

Several IANA ids share one stored zone, so the API can answer with the group's representative rather than with the id that was sent - `Europe/Rome` reads back as `Europe/Berlin`, same clock and same daylight-saving rules. The configured spelling is therefore kept, which also means a zone changed outside Terraform is not reported as drift.
- `to` (Number) When the window closes, in Unix seconds. Give the length once, as this or as `duration_sec`; whichever is written, the other is read back.

### Read-Only

- `created` (Number) When the window was created, in Unix seconds.
- `from_rfc3339` (String) `from` rendered in UTC, for reading. The API takes and publishes Unix seconds.
- `id` (String) The window's id.
- `overlimited` (Boolean) Whether the account's package has stopped this window from applying.
- `state` (String) Where the window is in its life: `scheduled`, `active` or `finished`.
- `to_rfc3339` (String) `to` rendered in UTC, for reading.
- `updated` (Number) When the window last changed, in Unix seconds. Maintenance windows stamp this on every edit.

<a id="nestedatt--monitors"></a>
### Nested Schema for `monitors`

Required:

- `monitor_id` (String) The monitor this entry covers, which must be the account's own.
- `suppress` (Attributes) What the window holds back for this monitor. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--monitors--suppress))

<a id="nestedatt--monitors--suppress"></a>
### Nested Schema for `monitors.suppress`

Optional:

- `alerts` (Boolean) Hold back this monitor's alerting.
- `stats` (Boolean) Keep this monitor's checks inside the window out of the statistics.



<a id="nestedatt--recurrence"></a>
### Nested Schema for `recurrence`

Optional:

- `week_days` (Set of String) The days it repeats on, by English name (`"Sunday"`), in the window's own time zone.


<a id="nestedatt--suppress"></a>
### Nested Schema for `suppress`

Optional:

- `alerts` (Boolean) Hold back alerting for the duration of the window.
- `stats` (Boolean) Keep the window's checks out of the uptime statistics, so planned downtime does not read as an outage.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A window created in the web app is adopted by its id, which the
# `hosttracker_maintenance_windows` data source publishes as `ids`.
terraform import hosttracker_maintenance.weekly_database 2c9a5f31-7b64-4e08-91d2-5a3c6e7b8f40
```
